camps.name: Lower Ptarmigan Ridge camp
camps.why: Gets the pack weight up out of Spray Park in one day and leaves a short drop onto the North Mowich Glacier; the lower Edmunds divide camp near 8,100 ft works the same way.

new_camps.name: Camp Schurman
new_camps.why: Where this carry-over ends: you top out on Liberty Cap and drop the Emmons side to the first established camp, then walk out to White River in the morning.
new_camps.notes: Ranger hut and solar toilet sit here, but the hut is not a shelter for climbers. Melt snow for water and register for the climb before you leave.

plan_conflict: The plan's night 2 is Camp Schurman (day 2 ends there), which is not on file; a party that skis or climbs and returns instead sleeps a second night at the 8,100 ft Edmunds divide camp.

camps.name: Curtis Ridge camp
camps.why: The launch point for the ridge: flat snow ground reached over St. Elmo Pass, a short approach to the climb and out of most rockfall lines.

camps.name: Camp Schurman
camps.why: Day 2 ends here after the Emmons-Winthrop descent; the ranger camp is the first flat, established ground, so most tired parties sleep before the walk out.

camps.name: White River Campground
camps.why: Drive-in campground at the trailhead; a night here the evening before gives an early start but is not part of the three-day plan.

plan_conflict: Camp Schurman was a route camp on file but is where day 2 ends, so it is now the night 2 main; strong parties can instead continue to White River the same night.

camps.name: Camp Muir
camps.why: Where nearly every party sleeps: shelter, a toilet and a ranger post, with the summit day starting right from the camp.

camps.name: Ingraham Flats
camps.why: A thousand feet higher, it shortens summit day but is colder, less sheltered, and sits under icefall; mostly an overflow or guided-trip option.

plan_conflict: Ingraham Flats was marked main on file; two mains for one night is wrong and parties on this route sleep at Camp Muir, so Flats is now a route camp.

camps.name: Camp Schurman
camps.why: The established high camp: ranger hut, toilet and the shortest summit day on the Emmons, so almost all parties sleep here.

camps.name: Emmons Flats
camps.why: A bench just above Schurman; quieter and a little higher, but you cross crevassed ground to reach the toilet and ranger post, so rope up between them.

camps.name: Glacier Basin
camps.why: Forested camp 3.5 miles in, used the night before a climb or when no Schurman permit is available; it adds a long, heavy day 1 to the summit push.

plan_conflict: Emmons Flats was marked main on file alongside Camp Schurman; Schurman is where most parties sleep, so Flats is now a route camp.

camps.name: Castle camps on Wapowety Cleaver
camps.why: The only established camp on this side below the route: rock-ring sites on the cleaver put the Finger within a few hours, but expect wind and no water.

camps.name: Camp Muir
camps.why: The standard base for the Ledges: sheltered ground, a toilet and a ranger post, and the route starts from the camp's own door.

camps.name: Ingraham Flats
camps.why: Sits on the wrong side of the Cowlitz Glacier for the Ledges; it only makes sense for parties continuing on the Cleaver, so skip it here.

camps.name: Camp Muir
camps.why: Where most parties sleep: the most sheltered ground on this side, with a toilet, ranger post and a hut for storms.

camps.name: Ingraham Flats
camps.why: Takes about 1,000 ft off summit day, but it is colder, has no toilet and sits under icefall; the plan's optional three-day variation.

plan_conflict: Ingraham Flats was marked main on file beside Camp Muir; the plan itself sleeps at Muir, so Flats is now the route option.

camps.name: Upper Castle
camps.why: Where most parties camp: large rock rings, water in warm weather, and a safer spot than Camp Hazard for the ice fall above it.

camps.name: Camp Hazard
camps.why: Highest regular camp; saves a long summit day but sits below the Kautz ice cliff, has narrow ledges, and often has no water.

camps.name: Lower Castle
camps.why: A few close rock rings on the same ridge; fine for a small party that arrives late, but it leaves about 300 ft more to climb in the morning.

camps.name: Wilson Moraine
camps.why: Lower moraine sites that lengthen summit day a lot; used only by parties starting late or lacking a bigger site higher.

camps.name: Rock Step bivy sites
camps.why: Tiny ledges by the notch above the Rock Step; a place to wait out weather, not a planned camp, and exposed to the ice cliff above.

plan_conflict: The plan ends day 1 at Camp Hazard, but guides and ranger reports say most climbers avoid it for ice fall and sleep at Upper Castle.

camps.name: Castle camps on Wapowety Cleaver
camps.why: Where most parties camp: sheltered rock rings and often running water, with the headwall about five hours above.

camps.name: Camp Hazard
camps.why: Shortens summit day by roughly 1,300 ft, but it sits below the Kautz ice cliff, offers narrow ledges and often no water; many climbers avoid it.

plan_conflict: The plan ends day 1 at Camp Hazard, which was marked main on file; guides say most climbers avoid it for ice fall and sleep at the Castle camps.

camps.name: Curtis Ridge
camps.why: Flat snow ground near the gully down to the Carbon, with little rockfall; camping here makes a short second day to Thumb Rock.

camps.name: Thumb Rock
camps.why: The only real camp on the ridge, with a tent platform on the saddle; it makes summit day a single push but gets rockfall and icefall.

camps.name: Edmunds/North Mowich glacier divide camp
camps.why: A camp of this kind at about 8,100 ft puts you on the correct side of the glacier and parties on the neighboring Mowich lines climb from it directly.

camps.name: Ptarmigan Ridge bivy above Observation Rock
camps.why: Best wind shelter on this side, but you still descend scree to the North Mowich Glacier in the morning, so a longer start to the face.

camps.name: High camp below the North Mowich headwall
camps.why: Closest to the face at about 10,000 ft, but fully exposed to ice and rock coming off the headwall; wear a helmet in camp.

camps.name: Liberty Cap saddle
camps.why: An emergency bivy for a benighted party after topping out, not a place to plan a night.

plan_conflict: The plan moves to a higher camp on night 2, but the reports found for the neighboring Mowich-side lines stayed at the 8,100 ft divide camp for every night; no Mowich Face report was found to confirm the plan's staging.

camps.name: Nisqually Glacier camp below the icefall
camps.why: Camping low lets you be through the icefall before the sun hits it; the site shifts each year with the glacier and moraine.

camps.name: Camp Muir
camps.why: Used by early ascent parties who slept at Muir and crossed over to the icefall; it adds a long traverse in the dark, so not the usual night.

camps.name: Ingraham Flats
camps.why: Higher bench on the standard route where the Nisqually joins; only useful as the camp for a party that descends to it after the climb.

camps.name: Curtis Ridge camp
camps.why: The usual first night: crest ground between the Winthrop and Carbon glaciers, near the point where parties cross to the ridge the next day.

camps.name: Ptarmigan Ridge high camp
camps.why: The camp the route is built around: bivy ground at about 10,300 ft on the crest, just outside the serac fall line and fully exposed to wind.

camps.name: Glacier Basin camp
camps.why: The last forested camp with bear boxes and a toilet; fine for a night before the approach but too low to be a night on the climb.

camps.name: Camp Schurman
camps.why: Reached after the Emmons-Winthrop descent on summit day; parties who stop for the night here make it a fourth night, which this plan does not include.

plan_conflict: Day 1 says camp partway up the Russell Glacier; trip reports and the camp on file place the first night on Curtis Ridge.

camps.name: Puyallup Cleaver high camp
camps.why: The usual high camp: it puts the climb a day's push away and the cleaver crest stays out of runnels, but it is wind-exposed.

camps.name: Colonnade Ridge
camps.why: A first stop above the Wonderland Trail that depends on snow cover; it makes a very long summit day, so it is rarely a plan.

camps.name: Open bivouac near 9,600 ft
camps.why: Cuts the summit day, but there is only what you dig; worth it only with firm snow for the face above.

camps.name: Bergschrund camp in the Sunset Amphitheater
camps.why: A small flat by the schrund; shortest summit day, but the headwall above sheds ice and rock, so pitch it with care.

new_camps.name: Klapatche Park
new_camps.why: The nearest official trail camp past St. Andrews Park; sleeping at the ridge foot keeps day 2 to the cleaver, but it books up on summer weekends.
new_camps.permit: A Wonderland Trail wilderness permit is needed for the night.
new_camps.notes: Elevation from the park's trip planner. The first night is not confirmed by a Sunset Ridge report, which is why confidence is low.

new_camps.name: Camp Muir
new_camps.why: The usual descent camp when coming down the standard route; shelter and a toilet, but no sign of what parties choose after this climb.
new_camps.notes: The plan's day 3 only says descend to a high camp and day 4 names Schurman or Muir, so which camp is not confirmed by a trip report.

plan_conflict: Night 1 (about 6,000 ft near St. Andrews Park) and night 3 (Schurman or Muir) have no camp on file and no Sunset Ridge report confirming either.

camps.name: Puyallup Cleaver camp below St. Andrews Rock
camps.why: Flat sites below the rock at the cleaver's top; the glacier is a short, quick day from here, so parties stay put for the summit night.

new_camps.name: Klapatche Park
new_camps.why: The closest trail camp past St. Andrews Park; a night here splits the long approach, but it fills on summer weekends.
new_camps.permit: A Wonderland Trail wilderness permit is needed for the night.
new_camps.notes: Elevation from the park's trip planner. The camp on file only says many parties spend the first night at St. Andrews Park, so the exact spot is not confirmed.

plan_conflict: Day 4 walks out to the car, so a night 4 does not exist; the first night's camp (St. Andrews Park area) is not on file.

camps.name: Curtis Ridge camp
camps.why: The launch point for the wall: you leave before midnight to reach the avalanche cones frozen, so sleep here and not on the Carbon Glacier floor.

camps.name: Glacier Basin camp
camps.why: Forested camp with a toilet and bear boxes; last reliable running water, but too low to be a night on this trip.

camps.name: St Elmo Pass bivy
camps.why: A staging bivy at the pass where parties rope up; useful when a late start makes the Curtis Ridge traverse too long for one day.

new_camps.name: Camp Schurman
new_camps.why: Day 2 ends here after the Emmons-Winthrop descent; it is the first established camp, though fit parties walk straight out.
new_camps.notes: Ranger hut and solar toilet; the hut is not a shelter for climbers.

plan_conflict: Day 3 walks out to the car, but day 2 ends at Camp Schurman and the camp is not on file, so it is added as the night 2 main.

camps.name: Point 6631 (base camp north of Pyramid Peak)
camps.why: A flat bench at the base of the cleaver reached in one day from Longmire, with water nearby and the cleaver starting right above.

camps.name: Cleaver crest col
camps.why: Best ground on the route: a broad saddle on the crest out of rockfall lines, with the summit push next, though it has no water.

camps.name: Devil's Dream camp
camps.why: Forested trail camp with reliable water that adds a night's gain to day 2; a bail-out or late start, not the usual night.

camps.name: Dug platform on the lower-mid cleaver
camps.why: For parties caught low on the cleaver; the dug platform is protected from the rockfall lines either side but exposed above you.
